<explanation>
Below is a step-by-step guide for drafting a precise system-architecture diagram of the Agent Development Kit (ADK) project. Use the project’s file tree and README to tailor these instructions to ADK’s particular components, flows, and integrations.

1. Identify the Project Type and Purpose
   • The ADK repo is an open-source, code-first Python toolkit (library) for building, evaluating, and deploying AI agents.  
   • It provides core abstractions (Agents, Tools, Callbacks, Workflows, Sessions, Context, Streaming), model- and deployment-agnostic adapters, and documentation/examples.

2. High-Level Architectural Layers
   Draw your diagram as a series of horizontal or concentric layers:
   a. Developer Layer  
      – Python application code (examples/, tutorials/, notebooks/)  
      – User-defined Agents, Tools, Custom callbacks  
   b. ADK Core Library Layer  
      – Core modules in the released package (`google_adk` namespace):  
        • Agents (llm_agents, custom_agents, workflow_agents)  
        • Tools (built_in, function_tools, openapi_tools, third_party)  
        • Callbacks (before/after model/tool/agent)  
        • Sessions & Context  
        • Streaming & Runtime  
        • Deployment connectors (Cloud Run, Vertex AI Agent Engine)  
   c. Model & Tool Adapters Layer  
      – LLM Providers (Gemini, OpenAI, Anthropic, etc.)  
      – Google-specific services (Search, Vertex AI, Cloud APIs)  
      – External APIs via OpenAPI specs or custom integration  
   d. Infrastructure & Services Layer  
      – Deployment targets (Cloud Run, GKE, Vertex AI Agent Engine)  
      – CI/CD pipelines (GitHub Actions: python-lint, python-tests, publish-docs)  
      – Documentation site build (mkdocs → site/)  
      – Artifact storage, monitoring, logging  

3. Extract Key Components from the File Tree
   • Top-level directories:  
     – docs/ → full Sphinx & MkDocs documentation, code examples  
     – examples/, notebooks/, tutorial code → demonstration of ADK usage  
     – .github/workflows/ → CI steps (lint, test, publish docs)  
     – mkdocs.yml + overrides/ + site/ → doc site generation pipeline  
   • README.md signals the core purpose & high-level features.

4. Relationships & Data Flows
   • Developer writes Python code against the ADK Core Library → instantiates Agents and Tools → submits tasks.  
   • ADK Core orchestrates calls to LLM adapters and external Tools → streams responses back through Callback hooks.  
   • Multi-agent workflows compose Agents in parallel/sequential/loop patterns.  
   • Output may be logged, persisted in Session/Context stores, or forwarded to downstream services.  
   • At build/deploy time, CI workflows test the library and examples, then publish docs to GitHub Pages via mkdocs.

5. Architectural Patterns & Principles
   • Modular design: clear separation of concerns (Agents vs. Tools vs. Callbacks vs. Deployments).  
   • Dependency injection / inversion: user code supplies tool definitions; library core orchestrates them.  
   • Extensibility points: custom agents, custom tools, custom callbacks.  
   • Pluggable adapters: interchangeable model and deployment backends.

6. Tailoring Guidelines for This Library-Tool Project
   • Emphasize the “core library” block with its sub‐modules.  
   • Show “extensibility ports” where user code injects custom Agents/Tools/Callbacks.  
   • Detail the “adapter layer” that routes calls to LLM providers or cloud APIs.  
   • Include the “deployment connectors” linking to Cloud Run/GKE and Vertex AI.

7. Diagramming Best Practices
   • Use clearly labeled boxes for each component (e.g., “Agent Module,” “OpenAI Adapter,” “Cloud Run”).  
   • Draw directional arrows:  
     – From user code → ADK Core → Adapters → External Services → back.  
     – From CI pipeline → docs build → GitHub Pages.  
   • Apply color coding:  
     – Library modules (blue)  
     – User artifacts (yellow)  
     – External services & infra (green)  
     – CI/CD and docs pipeline (gray)  
   • Use distinct shapes (e.g., cylinders for data stores like Session/Context, cloud icons for services).

8. Example Component Breakdown
   • Developer Workspace  
     – examples/, notebooks/, custom agents/tools code  
   • ADK Core  
     – google_adk.agents (llm, custom, workflow)  
     – google_adk.tools (built_in, function, openapi, third_party)  
     – google_adk.callbacks  
     – google_adk.runtime (sessions, context, streaming)  
   • Adapter Layer  
     – LLM connectors (Gemini, OpenAI, Anthropic)  
     – Google Cloud APIs (Search, Vertex AI, Cloud Run)  
   • Deployment Targets  
     – Cloud Run / GKE  
     – Vertex AI Agent Engine  
   • CI/CD & Docs  
     – GitHub Actions → python-lint/test → mkdocs → docs site

By following these steps and organizing each layer/component distinctly, your system design diagram will accurately reflect ADK’s architecture—showing how user code, the core library, adapters, and deployment infrastructure all interconnect.
</explanation>
